html:
Rhodesia was the name of the lands north and south of the Zambezi taken by Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company from 1890, and named after him in 1895. The map uses it for the whole region in 1914 and again in 1945.

The company sent its Pioneer Column onto the Shona plateau in 1890, conquered the Ndebele kingdom in 1893, and crushed the risings of 1896 and 1897. It hoped for a second Witwatersrand of gold, which never appeared, so it turned to settler farming and mining. North of the Zambezi it ruled through treaties with chiefs such as the Lozi king.

The company's rule ended in 1923 and 1924. The south became the self-governing settler colony of Southern Rhodesia and the north the protectorate of Northern Rhodesia. When the north became Zambia in 1964, the south took the name Rhodesia alone. Its white government declared independence under Ian Smith in 1965, fought the Bush War, and gave way to Zimbabwe in 1980.
sum: Rhodesia was the name of the lands north and south of the Zambezi taken by Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company from 1890, and named after him in 1895. The map uses it for the whole region in 1914 and again in 1945.
